perplexed: Not sure what to think or do; confused.
roundabout: A short jacket that fits close to the body. Boys wore it in the old days.
switch: A thin stick that bends easily. It was used to hit a child when he had done wrong.
hookey: Staying away from school when you should be there. 'Play hookey' means to do this.
knack: A special way of doing something well and easily.
ambuscade: A secret attack from a place where the attacker waits. Here, Aunt Polly waits for Tom in the dark.
lick: To beat someone in a fight, or to hit as a punishment. A 'lick' is a hit.
obleeged: A spoken spelling of 'obliged'. It means forced to do something.
whitewash: A white paint made of lime and water. People put it on fences and walls.
hollow: Empty, with no real happiness or meaning.
skylarking: Playing around in a loud and silly way.
taw: The big marble that a player shoots at the other marbles.
straitened: Small and not enough. Here, it is about the little money and few things that Tom has.
personating: Acting like another person or thing.
covet: To want something very much, especially something that is another person's.
balmy: Warm and soft in a nice way.
diluted: Made weaker by adding something. Here, she made her kind words less strong.
sally: To run out suddenly, to attack or to help.
morosely: In a sad way, in a bad mood.
beseeching: Asking in a very serious and worried way.
tallow: Hard animal fat. People made candles from it.
audacious: Bold; showing no fear of what other people think.
benediction: A prayer, often said at the end of a church meeting, asking for good things for the people.
scarify: To make small cuts or marks on something. Here, the new knife makes marks on the cupboard.
counterfeited: Copied to fool people. Here it means a false copy of a real Barlow knife.
disconcerted: Upset and confused because something went wrong.
galled: Made someone feel angry and hurt.
pew: A long seat made of wood, in a church.
cravat: A wide cloth that a man wears around his neck, like a tie.
wily: Clever in a way that fools people.
preposterous: Very silly; too strange to believe.
seductive: Very nice to think about, so that you want to go to it. Here, the summer outside pulls Tom away from church.
simpering: Smiling in a silly way that is not real.
tittering: Quiet laughing that you try to hide.
supplication: A humble and serious request, especially to God.
prosy: Boring because it is too long and too plain.
brimstone: A yellow stone that burns with a bad smell. 'Fire and brimstone' is about hell, in a hard sermon.
fillip: A quick push made with a finger that is first held back by the thumb and then let go.
vagrant: Going from place to place with no home.
canvassed: Looked at with care, one part after another. Here, Tom checks his body for signs of sickness.
mortified: In this story, said of a part of the body that has died and is going bad. Tom says this about his sore toe.
gaudy: Too bright and showy. Here, Tom likes Huck's wild life outside the rules.
spunk: In 'spunk-water', rain water that stays in an old rotten tree. The boys think it can take away warts.
wart: A small, hard bump on the skin.
ferule: A flat stick or ruler. A teacher used it to hit a pupil's hand.
gable: The top part of a house wall, with three sides, under the roof.
portentous: Looking very important and a little frightening.
jubilant: Very happy because something went well.
tick: A very small bug that bites. The boys play with one.
deftly: In a quick and clever way, with good use of the hands.
andiron: A metal stand that holds wood in a place for fire.
upbraid: To say angry words to someone, or to yourself, because of a wrong.
baffled: Made unable to understand or to carry on. Here, they thought that crossing water stopped anyone who followed.
grisly: Horrible and frightening to look at.
doublet: A short, tight jacket that men wore in past times.
cutlass: A short, heavy, curved sword used by sailors long ago.
shingle: A thin flat piece of wood, used on a roof.
caitiff: An old word for a bad person who is weak and has no courage.
lath: A thin, narrow piece of wood. The boys use laths as toy swords.
doodlebug: A small bug that lives in a hole in the sand. The boys think it can answer questions.
nettle: A plant with small hairs that hurt the skin.
ensconced: Settled in a safe place where nobody can see.
caterwauling: The loud, ugly sound that cats make at night.
deathwatch: A small bug that makes a clicking sound in wood. People thought it meant that someone would die.
ingenuity: The power to think of clever ways to do things.
fuddled: Mixed up in the mind, often because of drink.
ruffian: A rough man who hurts people.
tannery: A place where animal skins are made into leather.
verdigrease: The green poison that forms on brass or copper. Tom says a brass pin may have it on it.
escapade: An exciting adventure in which someone does what he should not do.
phase: A spoken spelling of 'faze': to trouble or upset someone.
ostentatiously: In a showy way, so that everyone sees.
palsy: An illness that makes the body shake and not obey.
miscreant: A bad person who does very wrong things.
coroner: An official who finds out how a person died. In the boys' game, the leader of a pretend meeting for a dead cat.
infatuated: Filled with a strong love for something that is not wise or good.
inveterate: Always doing something, as a habit, and not likely to stop.
quack: Not real. A 'quack' medicine does not work, and the people who sell it are not honest.
avariciously: With a strong wish to get something for yourself.
crestfallen: Sad and ashamed because things did not go as you wanted.
smouldering: Burning slowly, with smoke but no flame.
dauntless: Not afraid at all; cannot be made afraid.
sweetmeat: A sweet thing to eat, such as fruit with sugar on it.
freebooters: Pirates or robbers who take things from others by force.
quicksilver: A shining silver metal that is liquid. Today it is called mercury.
mutiny: When the crew of a ship will not obey the leader and act against him.
quartering: Moving across a river at a slant, not straight across.
ejaculations: Short, sudden cries or words said aloud.
weltering: Rolling or lying in something. Here, Tom is crying so much that he is lost in tears.
true-blue: Faithful; always true to his friends.
snifter: A small amount of strong drink, or of smoke. Joe says one little puff would be too much for Johnny Miller.
charily: Carefully, in a way that shows you are not sure.
hendering: A country spelling of 'hindering': stopping someone from doing something.
spume: White foam on water. 'Spumeflakes' are flakes of this foam.
scalped: Cut the skin and hair from the head of an enemy, as some warriors did long ago.
soliloquized: Spoke aloud to herself when alone.
pregnant: Full of meaning. Here, 'pregnant with prophecy' means full of hidden signs of what would happen.
funereal: Sad and slow, as at a funeral.
transfixed: Not able to move because of shock.
rascalities: Bad acts that are naughty or not honest.
cowhide: A strong whip made from the skin of a cow, used to beat people.
abashed: Ashamed and not knowing what to do.
slink: To go away quietly, because you feel ashamed.
artlessly: In a simple, honest way, with no plan to fool anyone.
humiliated: Feeling ashamed and made to look silly.
mercury: In 'a sudden falling of his mercury', it is the silver liquid in a tube that shows how warm it is. Here, Tom's good feeling goes down.
softy: A person who is too gentle and easy to fool.
lethargy: A heavy feeling of being tired, with no energy.
flaying: A very hard beating. Here, it is the teacher's beating of Tom.
retribution: A hard thing done to someone in return for a wrong.
dominie: A Scottish word for a schoolmaster.
mellow: Soft and easy in manner. Here, it is because of drink.
gawky: Tall and clumsy, not knowing how to move.
declamatory: In the style of a loud, formal speech.
unpalatable: Not nice to accept or hear.
voluptuous: Full of pleasure for the body and senses.
gilded: Covered with a thin layer of gold paint.
scuttle: A small opening with a cover, in a roof or floor.
minstrel: In this story, a show with songs and jokes by actors.
mesmerizer: A person who puts others in a sleep-like state to show tricks.
forbearance: Patience; not showing anger and not hitting back.
toils: A trap made of nets or ropes. Here, the law is closing around Potter like a trap.
deposed: Said in court, under a promise to tell the truth, what one knows.
diffident: Shy and not sure of yourself.
lynch: To kill a person by a crowd, without a court.
hieroglyphics: Pictures and signs used as writing. Huck and Tom say it as 'hy'roglyphics'.
sepulchral: Sounding deep and sad, like a voice from a grave.
ha'nted: A spoken spelling of 'haunted': visited by ghosts.
